title: Double the Recipe
briefing: Chef just told you the party of 12 became a party of 28. Scale the hollandaise, right now. No calculator.

expertRecipe.name: Hollandaise (Scaled)
expertRecipe.platingStandard: Smooth emulsion, no breaking, correct yield for cover count.

steps.instruction: Calculate new yield: 28 covers / 12 covers = 2.33x multiplier.
steps.whyExplanation: Wrong multiplier cascades through every ingredient. One math error = entire batch wasted.

steps.instruction: Scale egg yolks: 6 yolks x 2.33 = 14 yolks.
steps.whyExplanation: Eggs are the emulsifier. Too few and the sauce breaks; too many and it tastes eggy.

steps.instruction: Scale clarified butter: 1.5 lb x 2.33 = 3.5 lb.
steps.whyExplanation: Butter is the bulk. Under-scaling means short portions; over-scaling wastes expensive product.

steps.instruction: Scale acid (lemon juice): 2 oz x 2.33 = 4.66 oz, round to 4.5 oz.
steps.whyExplanation: Acid balances richness. Over-acidifying a batch this size ruins 28 plates.

steps.instruction: Execute: temper yolks, stream butter at 145F, hold at 140F.
steps.whyExplanation: Hollandaise is a TCS food. Below 140F = danger zone. Above 160F = scrambled eggs.

criticalControlPoints.consequence: Hollandaise in the danger zone grows bacteria rapidly. Discard after 2 hours.
